review_scope: Twelve full navigation fragments and feature declaration read, including the nested organization-settings include. Descriptive UI claims only; images, product variables, linked pages and rendered versions remain unresolved. No authority or enforcement inferred.

claims.statement: Pattern management navigation begins at the repository, organization or enterprise scope where the pattern was created.
Repository and organization pattern navigation uses the owning scope's Advanced Security settings; linked definition instructions remain separate dependencies.
Enterprise pattern navigation uses the Policies security area and Security features; this is not proof of effective enterprise permissions.
The editing navigation selects the pattern of interest under custom patterns in the secret-scanning area; pattern identity must not be confused with global enablement.
The GHES conditional directs enterprise navigation through profile Enterprise settings.
The non-GHES branch directs navigation to the enterprise, using the cloud Enterprises page as an example; the branches must not be rendered simultaneously.
Enterprise navigation includes selecting the Policies tab.
Enterprise policy navigation selects the security area whose label is supplied by a product variable; the variable is not resolved by this fragment review.
Organization navigation starts from the profile Organizations menu.
Organization-settings navigation first selects the organization and includes a second reusable for the Settings tab.
The nested organization-settings fragment provides a More-menu fallback when the Settings tab is not visible; visibility alone does not prove authorization.
Repository navigation starts at the repository main page.
Repository-settings navigation provides a More-menu fallback when the Settings tab is not visible; this does not bypass missing permissions.
The repository security navigation label branches on the security-and-quality-tab feature before selecting a product-variable security area.
The security-and-quality-tab feature declaration covers fpt and ghec and does not declare GHES; absence must be handled through the version resolver rather than inferred as feature availability.
